searchText: Is this the right place to talk about EIP-2718? probably, not sure if there is better channel Ok, I'll go ahead then. I'm implementing it and just want to make sure that there are no fields expected to be common between legacy transactions and enveloped transactions. They're fully general and, after deserialization, aren't in principal required to have nonces, tos, froms, signatures, or anything like that. Yes, that is correct. However, I implemented the envelope to still assume those constructs as it was the least disruptive to the existing code base That could make sense, pay the refactoring cost later when some crazy exotic tx doesn't end up using them? 😅 exactly 🙂 1559 at least won't have gas price, it instead will have two others. So pretty soon we are going to have something "crazy exotic". 😄 2930 only adds a field though. Yeah, I'm going to try to refactor it so the data model reflects full generality. curious to see what you come up with! > Ok, I'll go ahead then. I'm implementing it and just want to make sure that there are no fields expected to be common between legacy transactions and enveloped transactions. They're fully general and, after deserialization, aren't in principal required to have nonces, tos, froms, signatures, or anything like that. <@213672586264051717> All transactions will have a transaction type. That is the only guaranteed piece of data across all of them. Oh yeah, I guess I could model the legacy tx as having a transaction type of `Frontier` internally even though their serialized rep doesn't have the byte https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2972 I don't know if it will make it in yet, but this is the hope for where legacy transactions end up. It would be type 0 or 1, assuming those values aren't taken by the time that EIP lands.
